page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 1843 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 85,051.53 and efficient software compilation capabilities, as demonstrated by a Geekbench Clang compilation score of 39,975.0. Redis SET operations are highly performant at 62.24 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is relatively modest, with weaker results in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench single-core tests. Memory bandwidth remains average, reaching 176.14 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

The D48plds_v5 offers a cost-efficient hardware profile for highly parallelized workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores without requiring a large memory footprint. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for scale-out compute tasks, multi-threaded compilation, containerized microservices, and high-throughput key-value stores like Redis. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or single-threaded applications that depend heavily on high single-core clock speeds.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 1843 GB of local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by high stress-ng multi-core and software compilation benchmarks, alongside exceptional Redis SET throughput of 62.24 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, scoring lower in single-threaded tasks. This server is highly cost-efficient for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, and key-value databases that do not demand extensive memory allocations.
